\[
\begin{gathered}
Y' = w_R R' + w_G G' + w_B B' \qquad \text{(luma)},
\\[4pt]
Y' = f\!\left( w_R\, f^{-1}(R') + w_G\, f^{-1}(G') + w_B\, f^{-1}(B') \right) \qquad \text{(luminance)},
\\[4pt]
\text{method} = \text{luma709}
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(R', G', B'\): Stored sRGB values from 0 to 255
- \(Y'\): The gray value written to all three channels
- \(w_R, w_G, w_B\): Channel weights. They add up to 1.
- \(f\): The sRGB encoding function from IEC 61966-2-1. Its inverse decodes to linear light.

The gray value is a weighted sum of the three channels. BT.709 uses the weights 0.2126, 0.7152 and 0.0722. BT.601 uses 0.299, 0.587 and 0.114. The luma methods apply the weights to the stored, gamma-encoded values. The luminance method first decodes them to linear light, sums, and encodes the result again. The Operator tab shows the weights in use.
